justifications.durability: The prepublication verification is a genuine guard that I falsified: removing verify_directory_files(temporary_path, ...) lets bytes disagreeing with their declared digest become visible (the post-write check still raises, so the test's 'destination is None' assertion fails) — reproduced as the declared control at EXIT=1. The root-swap defence survives the seam: test_object_root_path_swap_cannot_redirect_materialization passes private_directory_factory and is now routed through publish_files, and the temp directory is always removed in the finally block on success, loss and exception alike.
justifications.evidence: Reproduced independently in a scratch tree extracted from the reviewed head: the five-file gate (test_content_store, test_machine_artifact, test_machine_artifact_concurrency, test_mast_artifact, test_layer_fetch) run as fresh processes gives 5+8+2+61+6 = 82 passed, 3 skipped, all EXIT=0, matching the reviewed manifest's headline; the declared negative control reproduces at EXIT=1 with one failing id. Gaps: the reviewed manifest records no baseline_suite arm and its after_suite covers only test_content_store, so the designed base-vs-head delta reads no base log.
justifications.fit: publish_files follows the module idiom (keyword-only factory seams, a Protocol-typed ContentFile) and carries no plan, sprint or version label; error vocabulary is unchanged (ContentStoreError lifted to MachineArtifactError by _lifted). Deduction: machine_artifact.py imports the two factory primitives with a redundant self-alias.
justifications.goal_fidelity: nova/database/content_store.py:553 publish_files(...) composes exactly the sequence s3 names: it pins the verified object root, allocates a private directory, writes the declared sources plus manifest, verifies the temporary directory, renames it into place with no-clobber (linux renameat2 RENAME_NOREPLACE via _publish_directory_no_replace), then re-verifies the visible root and the published manifest. Both consumers now call it: nova/imas/machine_artifact.py:751 (_publish_files) and nova/database/layer_fetch.py:133 (publish_files), and neither module assembles the pinned-root write and no-replace sequence directly (grep for _publish_directory_no_replace/_create_private_directory in layer_fetch returns nothing).
justifications.reuse: This is the reuse improvement the layer-fetch review flagged as a follow-on, deliberately retired: layer_fetch._publish_layer collapses from ~40 lines of publication orchestration to one publish_files call, and machine_artifact.materialize_machine_artifact drops ~80 inline lines to a single _publish_files call. Hashing, temporary-directory allocation, no-replace rename and verification all live in one place.
justifications.scope_discipline: The whole diff is four paths, each inside the reviewed manifest's declared write paths; no out-of-scope file is touched. The declared write paths also name an evidence fragment and a figures directory that this refactor rung did not need, and none was written.
